title: Greymoor 21-Day Experiment — Kickstart Canvas & Success Hypotheses
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures the kickoff plan, measurable hypotheses, and an experiment-first activation roadmap for Greymoor Retail’s 21-day POC. The goal: validate whether Redwood inference can reduce average retrieval-to-response latency for product search assist features while keeping weekly inference cost under Greymoor’s threshold and maintaining NPS-style satisfaction >= 4.0 from inside beta users.

Context / why this matters:
- Greymoor runs a hybrid search + LLM assistant on product pages. Their current infra has spiky latency during sales events and cost per query is higher than their target.
- They want a short, low-risk experiment to confirm improvements in latency, cost, and helpfulness before committing to Dedicated capacity.

Primary success hypothesis (H1):
- Substantial reduction in 95th-percentile tail latency for assistant responses from 1.2s to <= 450ms for single-turn queries under normal load, while maintaining mean token cost reduction >= 30% versus current baseline.

Secondary hypotheses:
- H2: End-user helpfulness score (surveyed internal beta users) increases >= 0.5 points on a 5-point scale.
- H3: Retry/failure rate drops below 0.2% with Redwood’s fallback policy enabled.
- H4: Prefix/KV caching will reduce token throughput by >= 20% for repeat-session flows.

Key success metrics (what we will measure):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 response latency for assistant endpoints (ms).
- Cost: average token cost per session and projected monthly cost at production QPS.
- Quality: internal helpfulness survey average (0-5), top-5 intent classification accuracy on eval set.
- Reliability: error rate, retry count, fallback invocations.
- Operational: warm-up time, cold-start rate, and throughput achieved per GPU profile.

Acceptance criteria (POC pass conditions):
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms and p99 <= 900ms for baseline QPS (defined below).
- Cost: projected monthly inference cost <= Greymoor target (they provided $28k/month for current volume) with savings >= 20%.
- Quality: helpfulness >= 4.0 average AND no more than 3% drop in top-5 intent accuracy compared to their offline model.
- Reliability: less than 0.5% error rate and graceful fallback triggers < 0.2% of total requests.

Baseline definitions and assumptions:
- Baseline QPS: 60 sustained QPS with 300 QPS peak for flash events (as reported by Greymoor analytics).
- Test fixture: production-like recording of recent 72h traffic sample (anonymized) for replay.
- Models: compare current on-prem LLM + search stack vs Redwood-hosted model variants and a 4-bit quantized local variant in Redwood Private.

Kickoff workshop agenda (90 minutes) — recommended participants: Greymoor PM, Greymoor Eng lead, Solutions SE, Applied ML lead, Infra SRE, and Support SME:
- 0–10m: Introductions, success criteria review (this doc).
- 10–25m: Walkthrough of Greymoor call flows, authentication, and telemetry endpoints.
- 25–45m: Traffic profile and risk areas (peak days, cache hit expectations).
- 45–65m: Experiment plan: staging endpoints, traffic replay approach, canary rollout policy, and fallback designs.
- 65–80m: Instrumentation and dashboards: what we need from Greymoor (headers, sampling, session ids), and Redwood Console setup.
- 80–90m: Next steps and owner assignments.

21-day activation roadmap (high level):
- Day 0–2: Prep
  - Create staging keys, wire minimum telemetry (request id, session id, user-agent), share example payloads.
  - Import anonymized traffic sample into the experiment runner.
  - Redwood: provision test model variant and create initial console dashboards.
- Day 3–6: Dry-run / replay
  - Run traffic replay at 10–20% of baseline QPS. Monitor latency and correctness.
  - Iterate on batching/sequence length caps and quantization settings.
- Day 7–10: Canary (live)
  - Open canary to 2% live traffic for non-critical cohorts (logged-in beta users).
  - Measure p95 latency and fallback rate, validate helpfulness via in-app micro-survey.
- Day 11–16: Ramp
  - Gradually increase to 20% then 50% traffic depending on metrics.
  - Test autoscaling policies and observe cold-start behavior on burst loads.
- Day 17–20: Stress and failover testing
  - Simulate peak-day events (replay at 2x peak) and validate routing fallbacks and Dedicated burst behavior.
- Day 21: Wrap / decision
  - Produce final report with measured metrics, cost projection, and recommended next step (Dedicated trial, Private deployment, or opt-out).

Roles & owners (Day 0 assignments):
- Greymoor PM: product acceptance and user sampling for surveys.
- Greymoor Eng: provide telemetry schema, deploy small client toggle for canary.
- Solutions SE (Maya): lead experiment config, runbooks, weekly sync.
- Applied ML (Ethan): quality guardrails and eval set.
- SRE (Rina): define SLA targets and emergency rollback steps.

Instrumentation checklist (what we need from Greymoor):
- Request ID and session ID attached to all assistant API requests.
- Sampling hook for recording full request/response for 1% of requests.
- Post-call micro-survey popup for helpfulness (persist anonymized results).
- Access to a daily aggregated CSV of query volumes by route and response size.

Risk register / mitigations:
- Risk: PII in recorded requests. Mitigation: Greymoor must redact PII or use their own anonymization script before providing sample.
- Risk: Flash traffic creating billing surprises. Mitigation: strict quota and automatic throttling during canary; engineering alert at 2x baseline spend projection.
- Risk: Quality regression after quantization. Mitigation: maintain a quality hold (stop ramp) if helpfulness drops >0.5 or top-5 accuracy drops >3%.

Experiment evaluation template (to be filled at Day 21):
- Measured p50/p95/p99 (staging vs live canary vs baseline).
- Token cost per session and projected monthly spend.
- Helpfulness survey results (N and mean).
- Failures and fallback stats.
- Observed cold-starts and autoscaling events.
- Engineering friction notes (how many API changes required, infra cleanup estimate).

Decision rubric (recommended next-steps):
- If all acceptance criteria met: propose Dedicated 3-month reserved trial + SLA onboarding checklist.
- If latency/cost met but quality degraded: recommend Private deployment with model tuning + second 21-day iteration.
- If reliability or costs exceed target: recommend rollback and close POC; capture learnings for re-try.

Open questions for Greymoor (to answer before Day 3):
1) Can you share the anonymization tool we should run on the 72h traffic sample?
2) Are there hard token-cost ceilings per session we need enforced?
3) Which user cohorts should be excluded from canary? (e.g., premium shoppers)
4) Any compliance constraints around long-term logs retention?

Quick runbook for Day 1 (practical checklist):
- Confirm staging API keys and confirm test ping succeeds.
- Upload anonymized traffic sample to experiment runner.
- Create Redwood Console workspace and import baseline dashboards.
- Enable sampling for 1% request recording and confirm logs flow into S3.
- Schedule 30-min sync the next morning to review initial replay metrics.

Notes / rough estimates:
- Expected initial perf delta on hosted Redwood variant: p95 ~ 300–500ms depending on batch settings.
- Anticipated engineering changes: small client toggle + header enrichment (~2 engineer-days).
- Budget guard: enable billing alerts at 35% above projected baseline.

Attachments and artifacts to produce during experiment:
- day-0: telemetry spec, sample payloads, console link (created by Maya).
- day-7: early canary report and helpfulness micro-survey results.
- day-21: final experiment report + recommendation.

Next steps (owners):
- Maya: schedule kickoff workshop (target 2025-09-05) and create initial dashboards.
- Greymoor Eng (owner TBD): run anonymization, upload traffic sample by 2025-09-04.
- Ethan: prepare eval set and quality guard scripts by 2025-09-06.

Comments / notes to self:
- Keep instrumentation minimal to avoid lengthy approvals at Greymoor.
- Prefer live canary cohorts to be opt-in users only.
- Track incremental infra changes as separate Jira tickets (link to ENG-1427).

-- end of canvas --
